channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Doctors working in Bo'zatov and Taxtako'pir in Karakalpakstan to receive up to 200% bonus
item.description: Doctors working in Bo'zatov and Taxtako'pir in Karakalpakstan will receive bonuses of up to 200%. A University Medical Cluster will be established by integrating the Medical Academy, Children's Clinic, and Oncology Center into a unified system.

item.title: Group arrested in Tashkent for illegally providing SAT certificates
item.description: Authorities in Tashkent have busted a group, including university students, for illegally obtaining international SAT certificates for applicants. They operated a 'bunker' where IT specialists remotely solved test questions for candidates, charging $1,500 per certificate.

item.title: Uzbekistan begins construction of world's largest wind power station worth $2.6 billion
item.description: Construction has begun on a 1.5 GW wind power station in northwestern Uzbekistan, a $2.6 billion project with Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power. It will be the world's largest, featuring 1,500 km of power lines and three substations to connect to the national grid.

item.title: Uzbekistan to purchase 10 Škoda electric trains for city routes costing 157 million euros
item.description: Uzbekistan will acquire 10 Škoda 25Ev electric trains, each with four carriages, for city routes. The project, approved by the Tashkent City Council of People's Deputies, is planned for 2026-2030. New trains will feature a capacity of 432 seats, a service life of 30 years, and a maximum speed of 160 km/h.

item.title: Private kindergartens in Karakalpakstan to receive 7% loans with 5-year grace period
item.description: Private kindergartens in Karakalpakstan will be eligible for 7% loans over 15 years, including a five-year grace period. In other regions, loan interest rates will range from 7% to 15%, depending on proximity to the center.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Braces for Upcoming Flu and ARVI Season
item.description: Kyrgyzstan anticipates a seasonal rise in ARVI and flu cases starting late September or early October, according to the National Public Health Institute director. Health officials urge citizens to prepare for the epidemic season.

item.title: Uzbek President Assigns Regional Governors Task to Develop Karakalpakstan Neighborhoods
item.description: Uzbek President tasked regional governors to develop assigned neighborhoods in Karakalpakstan. A proposal was made to name streets and neighborhoods after the regions that improved them, if residents approve. Residents will evaluate the improvements.

item.title: Chinese agricultural delegation explores Dangara district's potential in Tajikistan
item.description: A delegation from China's Ministry of Agriculture visited Tajikistan's Dangara district to strengthen bilateral cooperation. They examined the district's agricultural potential, production capabilities, and agrarian sector development. Discussions focused on expanding cooperation, attracting investment, and sharing experiences in agriculture.

item.title: Entrepreneurs in Karakalpakstan to receive 12% loans, with 4% subsidized
item.description: Entrepreneurs in Karakalpakstan will be eligible for 12% loans, with the Entrepreneurship Development Company covering 4% of the interest rate. The responsible bank will open a 300 billion soum credit line for reliable clients.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Prime Minister and staff clean up Boz-Boltock mountain
item.description: The Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan and presidential administration staff participated in a nationwide cleanup event on Boz-Boltock mountain in the Alamedin district. Participants removed solid waste, emphasizing the importance of environmental care and citizen responsibility.

item.title: Karakalpakstan to become a major 'green' energy production hub, says President Mirziyoyev
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced Karakalpakstan is set to become a major 'green' energy production center. New energy capacities totaling 860 MW have been commissioned, increasing electricity production fourfold. The region's share of green energy reached 23% with new wind farms.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Manufacturing Sector Output Reaches Nearly 476 Billion Som
item.description: From January to August 2026, Kyrgyzstan's manufacturing industry produced goods worth 475.966 billion som, a 10.1% increase year-on-year. Chemical production saw the largest growth, increasing 2.3 times. Significant increases were also noted in coke, refined petroleum products, machinery, automobiles, and basic metals.

item.title: Tashkent-Nukus high-speed train to launch in March, Karakalpakstan to host $8 billion AI projects
item.description: The Tashkent-Nukus high-speed train service will commence in March of next year. Additionally, Karakalpakstan is set to implement projects worth $8 billion focused on artificial intelligence and data centers.

item.title: El Niño may trigger new crisis in some Asian countries, research suggests
item.description: El Niño could pose a risk of a new crisis in several Asian nations, according to research. The conflict in Iran is exacerbating the situation by negatively impacting fuel and fertilizer supplies crucial for agriculture.

item.title: Tashkent-Nukus high-speed train service to be launched in March 2027
item.description: The Tashkent-Nukus high-speed train service will be launched in March 2027, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced. Travel time will be reduced from 16 to 7 hours. The meeting also discussed infrastructure development and new social facilities in Karakalpakstan.

item.title: 3.3 GW Wind Power Plants to Launch in Karakalpakstan, Aiming for 76% Green Energy by 2030
item.description: Karakalpakstan plans to launch 3.3 gigawatt wind power plants, aiming to increase the share of "green" energy to 76% by 2030. The region also plans to create 400 megawatts of energy storage capacity.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva: Investments in Karakalpakstan are Growing, New Significant Projects Emerging
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva stated that investments in Karakalpakstan are increasing, with new significant projects emerging. She noted that the launch of major projects in energy, industry, transport, and other sectors, often with foreign partners, confirms confidence in the country and its favorable business conditions.

item.title: CIS Anti-Corruption Council holds 11th meeting in Minsk, discusses asset confiscation
item.description: The 11th meeting of the CIS Interstate Council for Combating Corruption took place in Minsk. Delegations from Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Russia participated. Discussions covered modern anti-corruption methods, asset confiscation, and innovative technologies.

item.title: Waste processing plants with a total capacity of 454 million kWh to be built in Surxondaryo, Bukhara, and Karakalpakstan
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to build waste processing plants in three regions: Surxondaryo, Bukhara, and Karakalpakstan. These facilities will generate electricity through thermal waste processing, with a total capacity of 454 million kWh. The projects aim to attract $395 million in direct investment.

item.title: Active phase of CSTO joint exercise 'Rubezh-2026' concludes in Kazakhstan
item.description: The active phase of the joint exercise 'Rubezh-2026' involving the Collective Rapid Deployment Forces of the Central Asian region (CRDF CSTO) has concluded in Kazakhstan. The drills simulated blocking and destroying illegal armed formations and restoring border security.

item.title: Tajikistan Interdepartmental Commission Discusses Aviation Security Measures
item.description: An interdepartmental commission meeting on civil aviation security was held in Dushanbe, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Usmonali Usmonzoda. The meeting aimed to coordinate efforts to prevent and neutralize threats to passengers, crew, and aviation infrastructure. The commission meets at least twice a year.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov arrives in the USA for a working visit
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has arrived in the U.S. state of Utah for a working visit. He was met at the airport in Salt Lake City by Senate President Stuart Adams. Japarov will then travel to New York to attend the UN General Assembly's high-level week and hold bilateral meetings.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: New decree allows entry into civil service without competition for certain groups
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has amended rules for forming a civil service personnel reserve. Citizens with disabilities, graduates of specific lyceums and foreign programs, and distinguished graduates of Kyrgyz universities can now enter the reserve without competition if they meet qualifications. Rules for rotation and application submission have also been clarified.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Strengthens Sanctions Control for Domestic Protection
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is enhancing its sanctions control primarily to protect its own banks, investors, and businesses, not solely to meet foreign demands. The Minister of Economy stated the goal is to maintain economic activity within legal frameworks, avoid sanctions circumvention, and protect financial institutions from secondary sanctions risks.

item.title: New modern building material production expands in Karakalpakstan
item.description: A new enterprise, "Coals KS," in Nukus, Karakalpakstan, is expanding its production of modern building materials like gas blocks and lime. The $16.3 million project utilizes local raw materials and aims to supply both domestic and export markets, including Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan. The facility currently employs 200 local residents.

item.title: Modern thermal insulation materials produced in Nukus from local basalt
item.description: The "Nukus Insulation Group" enterprise in Nukus, Karakalpakstan, is producing modern thermal insulation materials from local basalt. The $50 million project, equipped with European technology, can produce 50,000 tons annually, meeting international standards. It creates 150 new jobs and enhances building energy efficiency.

item.title: Tashkent Metro undergoes significant expansion and modernization over the past decade
item.description: The Tashkent Metro has seen substantial development, adding 33 kilometers of new lines and 21 stations in recent years, expanding its network to 71 kilometers and 50 stations. Modernization efforts include new trains, digital payment systems, and improved safety and convenience for over a million daily passengers.

item.title: Tashkent Real Estate Fraud: Izmir Art Stroy Head Arrested, New Company to Continue Construction
item.description: Tashkent authorities have arrested the head of Izmir Art Stroy LLC amid an investigation into alleged fraud. The company is accused of taking over 287 billion soums from 1,530 citizens for apartments in unfinished housing complexes. A new company will now complete the construction projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Sign Cooperation Program to Combat Corruption
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia have approved a cooperation program to combat corruption for 2027-2028. The agreement, signed by the Prosecutor General of Russia and the Director of Uzbekistan's Anti-Corruption Agency, includes exchanging experience, implementing digital tools for risk identification, developing anti-corruption culture, and fostering scientific and educational collaboration.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan Discuss Migration Issues
item.description: The Ambassador of Kyrgyzstan to Kazakhstan, Kudaybergen Bazarbaev, met with the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan, Mukhtar Tileuberdi, to discuss bilateral cooperation. Key topics included implementing tasks set by the heads of state to elevate relations and creating favorable conditions for the stay, transit, and employment of citizens from both countries.

item.title: South Korea's Pragmatic Partnership Strengths in Central Asia Highlighted by Experts
item.description: Experts note South Korea's key advantage in Central Asia lies in its blend of technological capacity, investment potential, and practical modernization experience. Unlike many external players, South Korea's own economic development journey makes its expertise highly relevant for Central Asian nations seeking diversification and industrial growth. Its ability to adapt solutions to specific needs and its perceived neutral, pragmatic stance are significant strengths.

item.title: Uzbek President Inspects Mahalla Infrastructure Improvements and Income Generation Projects
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the "Diyqan arna" mahalla in Nukus district, Karakalpakstan, to review infrastructure upgrades and initiatives aimed at boosting residents' income. The "Smart Mahalla" system utilizes digital technologies for citizen services and infrastructure monitoring. Projects include a new kindergarten, sports facilities, and a focus on beekeeping as a primary income source for households.

item.title: Over 20 Companies Undergoing Bankruptcy Procedures in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: According to Kamil Chotkaraev, deputy director of the bankruptcy department at Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy and Commerce, 29 enterprises are currently undergoing bankruptcy proceedings. Since the start of 2026, 38 court decisions have been received, with nine companies closed and 29 still in the process. The number of bankrupt enterprises has decreased from approximately 375 to 227.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches Projects Worth $7.5 Billion in Karakalpakstan
item.description: During his visit to Karakalpakstan, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev launched 11 projects valued at $592 million and initiated 47 projects worth $7 billion. These initiatives are expected to create 8,000 jobs. Projects included wind power stations, a hospital built with UAE partnership, and a digital computing center.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Japanese Companies Discuss New Investment Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov met with the chairman of Keidanren and leaders of major Japanese companies to discuss economic cooperation. Discussions focused on expanding interaction, creating favorable conditions for foreign firms, and implementing new investment projects in energy, transport, infrastructure, and other sectors.

item.title: Italy to Deploy Warships to Bab al-Mandab Strait for Commercial Shipping Safety
item.description: Italy will deploy warships to the Bab al-Mandab Strait to ensure the safe passage of commercial vessels. The move aims to prevent disruptions to global and European economies that could arise if the strategic waterway is blocked, particularly by Houthi forces.

item.title: Over 3,000 Kyrgyz citizens expelled from Russia since start of year
item.description: Since the beginning of the year, 3,598 citizens of Kyrgyzstan have been expelled from Russia due to violations of migration laws. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported that 233 Kyrgyz citizens, including 48 women, are currently held at the 'Sakharovo' center. Approximately 10 citizens are planned for repatriation soon.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan Sign Energy Cooperation Roadmap
item.description: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan have signed a roadmap to expand energy cooperation for 2026-2028. The agreement, signed in Baku by energy ministers Sherzod Khodjayev and Parviz Shahbazov, focuses on implementing a green energy corridor, developing oil and gas exploration, and increasing oil product supplies. SOCAR's expansion in Uzbekistan is also a priority.

item.title: Uzbek President Inspects Nukus Insulation Group's European Equipment
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the Nukus Insulation Group enterprise. The facility, valued at $50 million, is equipped with modern European machinery. This allows for the production of goods meeting international standards using local raw materials.

item.title: Qaraqalpaqstan Launches $7.6 Billion Projects, Starts New Power Plant Construction
item.description: Qaraqalpaqstan has launched projects worth $7.6 billion and initiated the construction of new power generation facilities. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended the ceremony. These initiatives are expected to create 8,000 high-paying jobs.
